title: Finite-free coefficient bases and the chain-level sections-tensor comparison at the point
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\Ql$ inside $\Qlb$, with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $d=[L:E]$, and $R_F=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,s}$ for $F=E,L$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Sections mean evaluation at the final object $s\to s$ of $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Constant values give ring isomorphisms $\mathcal O_F\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(s,R_F)$, compatible with coefficient inclusions and with every finite quotient projection. The $R_E$-module sheaf $R_L$ has a basis $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ whose global sections, under these isomorphisms, are an $\mathcal O_E$-basis of $\mathcal O_L$.

For every sheaf $F$ of $R_E$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the balanced map
$$\theta_F:\Gamma(s,F)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L\longrightarrow\Gamma(s,F\otimes_{R_E}R_L),\qquad n\otimes a\longmapsto n\otimes a_s,$$
where $a_s$ is the constant-value section and the tensor on the right is the image under sheafification [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], is an $\mathcal O_L$-linear isomorphism, natural in $F$. Under the coordinate isomorphism $F\otimes_{R_E}R_L\cong F^{\oplus d}$, given locally by $f\otimes\sum_i r_i b_i\mapsto(r_if)_i$, $\theta_F$ is the identity on $\Gamma(s,F)^{\oplus d}$; its inverse sends $(n_i)_i$ to $\sum_i n_i\otimes b_i$. The map $\theta_F$ itself is independent of the chosen basis and uniquely determined by its pure-tensor formula. Both $F\mapsto F\otimes_{R_E}R_L$ and $N\mapsto N\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$ are additive exact functors (exactness of the sheaf functor is detected after restriction to $R_E$). Applied termwise, the maps $\theta_F$ commute with differentials and give natural isomorphisms of cochain complexes. No discreteness of $R_F$ or sectionwise formula for arbitrary sheaf tensor products is assumed.

proof.text: The absolute values on $E$ and $L$ agree on $E$ by uniqueness in [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value]. Choose an $\mathcal O_E$-basis $\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_d$ of $\mathcal O_L$ by [lem-sfb-local-field-integral-basis]. Apply [lem-pur-connected-adic-integral-basis] to $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, whose underlying space is a singleton. Its constant-value isomorphisms give $\Gamma(s,R_H)=\mathcal O_H$ with all quotient and inclusion compatibilities, and its prescribed columns $b_i=(\beta_i)_s$ give exactly the required sheaf/global basis. In Lean, form the integral basis as a linear equivalence from the bijective finite-sum map of Padic.exists_integral_basis, with its cardinality equal to the relative degree. The implementation reuses the proved private integral_basis helper of CompletedIntegralFiniteFree, whose proof is the same integral-basis existence argument; no completed finite-free comparison theorem is assumed for this step.

source.place: Lemmas 4.2.12 and 6.8.2(1), pp. 58-59; explicit common-global-basis sections calculation extracted from old proof steps 1-2 of lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension, supporting the final paragraph of def-weil-finite-coefficient-point

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-based-sheaf-tensor-evaluation] on $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$, with $R=R_E$, $S=R_L$, the coefficient map, the basis just constructed, and $U=s$. Transport its balanced map along the two constant-value ring isomorphisms. It sends $n\otimes a$ to $[n\otimes a_s]$, hence is exactly $\theta_F$. Its coordinates and inverse are the asserted ones; naturality, linearity, uniqueness and basis independence follow with the same formula. The sheaf tensor has the stated local coordinates because the presheaf tensor is already a sheaf. Use the generic theorem with independent site and coefficient universes. Transport its canonical change-of-rings functor to completedOrdinaryScalarExtension using the object and map equations, and transport evaluation across both coefficient ring equivalences by a semilinear tensor congruence. The global sheaf-basis equation identifies the scalar coordinates with those of the integral basis. Summing these coordinates proves the inverse formula, and pure tensors prove uniqueness.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; generic finite-basis evaluation comparison

proof.text: The exactness assertions of [lem-pur-based-sheaf-tensor-evaluation] apply to $R_E\to R_L$ with the sheaf basis of step 1 and to $\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_L$ with its integral basis. They give both additive exact functors and detection of sheaf exactness under restriction. Its termwise complex comparison at $U=s$, transported by step 1, has components exactly $\theta_{K^j}$ by step 2. Thus it gives the claimed natural isomorphism of complexes, including the asserted inverse, for arbitrary cochain complexes. For ordinary modules in the possibly larger section universe, tensor coordinates give a natural isomorphism between extension followed by restriction and the finite-power functor. Restriction reflects finite limits, so this proves preservation of finite limits without equating module and coefficient universes. Extend/restrict adjunction gives additivity and finite colimits. Apply NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex to the constructed natural comparison.
